surfaces.part: white cap on top of the sign head
sign head: teal band with ring symbol and yellow numbered panel (vertical faces)

answer.evidence: The sign head is a flat front-facing panel. A white cap sits on rows 0-2 with widths 6, 8, 8, then 10 from row 3. It widens steadily and is rounded only at its upper edge with a flat bottom, so it is a hat and not an ellipse plate. The teal row 3 and dark row 4 read as an outline and rim, not a top surface with a front-edge line. Rows 5-18 are the vertical face of the ring symbol and the yellow '1' panel. The pole (rows 20-26, width 6) widens to a 12-wide base (rows 27-31), which is a plain front view with no top plane. The result is front elevation with only a 2-row rim and no elliptical cap.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin pole sign with a small head and number plate. It measures 9 visible tones per tile, above bus-shelter-a (6) and just below kiosk-a (12), though well under vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0% and none of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is tinted dark blue-grey, which matches the references' treatment. It reads as a clean, small prop with no flat fills, but it has about 4 shading steps on the pole and sign and little grain, so it looks a bit thinner than the kiosk and vending references. For a sparse, thin object this is close to acceptable, but with only slight texture and fewer ramp steps than the richer references I would not pass it next to them.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin pole sign with a small number-plate head, so sparseness alone shouldn't count against it.
